title: Context Engineering SF: Advanced Context Engineering for Agents - Dex Horthy
summary: Dex Horthy on advanced context engineering: frequent intentional compaction, research/plan/implement, reviewing specs instead of code.

assertions.quote: our goal all the time is to keep context utilization under 40%

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: I think slash compact is trash. I never use it

verdicts.note: Fresh context avoids accumulated noise, but compaction is useful when state is hard to reconstruct; it is a tradeoff, not a rule.

assertions.quote: we have it write out a progress file very specifically

verdicts.note: External notes/memory files are a standard, effective pattern (Anthropic, Manus write-ups) for long tasks; adds retrieval overhead.
Subagents return summaries rather than raw exploration; Anthropic reports gains from multi-agent research, at higher token cost.

assertions.quote: we have three phases research, plan and implement

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.

assertions.quote: I still read all the tests, but I no longer read every line of code because I read the specs and I know they're right

verdicts.note: Plan review catches costly errors early and helps team alignment, but plans don't guarantee the code matches; most guidance and defect data still favor reviewing code, especially for security.

assertions.quote: a bad line of research ... can be thousands of bad lines of code

verdicts.note: The classic cost-of-defects gradient applies: requirement and design errors propagate; agents amplify this by generating large amounts of code from a flawed plan.

assertions.quote: it just doesn't work for complex tasks or brownfield tasks ... it can actually slow people down

verdicts.note: Consistent across Stanford's data, METR's mature-repo slowdown and long-context degradation results.
METR names repo size and maturity (10+ years, more than 1M lines) and complex edits as factors behind the slowdown, in contrast with greenfield RCTs that found speedups.
